title: Hyperbolic neural population geometry benefits computation
claim: Stimulus encoding through tuning curves induces a latent hyperbolic geometry, and decoding is realized as memory retrieval within that space.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, colored rounded boxes with titled stages
description: Four pastel rounded panels read left to right, each with a large title. (a) Pink 'Stimulus Space (Euclidean)' shows an oval arena with a mouse, overlapping colored place fields, a dotted walking path, and stacked colored firing traces over time. (b) Beige 'Tuning Curve (Encoder)' shows three Gaussian tuning curves of different widths, an arrow to 'Neuron Representation', and the vector λ(s). (c) Mint 'Latent Space (Hyperbolic)' lists the assumptions and definitions (uniform stimulus, overlap O_ab, semi-metric d_ab). A small tree is drawn turning into a hyperbolic tripod shape through an arrow marked 'Approx.'. (d) Blue 'Associative Memory (Decoder)' gives the decoding loss formula and a teal heatmap with orange memory squares, a red star query, and a diagonal trajectory. A dashed blue arrow links the loss to the trajectory and a legend sits at the right. The eye goes first to the four bold titles.
caption: (a) Illustration of the stimulus space $\pS$ and place cell firing patterns. (b) Illustration of how neurons encode stimulus $s$ through tuning curves $\lambda$ and output $n(s)$. (c) Our constructed tuning curve model that induces hyperbolic geometry.\ (d) Illustration of how the MMSE estimator (decoder) is realized by the memory retrieval dynamics in latent hyperbolic space.
abstract: Neural population geometry shapes downstream computation. Recent empirical findings in neurobiology suggest that a hyperbolic structure underlies population activity in the hippocampus. Here we provide a theoretical framework for this phenomenon. First, we propose a plausible construction of hippocampal tuning curves that statistically induces hyperbolic geometry. Next, we establish a connection between neural decoding and associative memory by demonstrating that the Modern Hopfield Network update rule computes the minimum mean-squared-error (MMSE) estimator. Finally, we introduce a novel associative memory model defined in hyperbolic space that yields significantly larger capacity than leading models. Our results suggest that animals encode spatial information as a latent hyperbolic cognitive map, improving both memory capacity and decoding accuracy.
